origin.description: Integer hash of each string in a character vector. Used for randomized experiments and feature hashing.

arguments.name: seed
arguments.text: Integer initial state. A different seed produces a different hash of the same string.

origin.details: Each string is hashed with Jenkins's one-at-a-time hash. The C loop reads a signed char and stops at the first zero byte. The unsigned 32-bit result is stored in an integer vector, so values at or above 2^31 are negative.
origin.value: An integer vector of the same length as x.
origin.example: digest2int("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", 0L)

translation.description: Integer hash of each string. A single string is a one-element result.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings. None is NA_character_ and hashes as the bytes of "NA".

arguments.name: seed
arguments.text: Passed through as.integer, then used as the uint32 starting state. Only the first value is used.

translation.details: Bytes above 127 are added as a signed char, and a zero byte ends the key. The uint32 hash is returned as a signed 32-bit int. A length-1 input is a one-element list.
translation.value: A list of ints, one per string.
translation.example:
from digest import digest2int
print(digest2int("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", 0))
